chapters.summary: This chapter records the genealogy and birth of Jesus Christ, showing that he is the descendant of Abraham and the son of David, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy.
keyPoints: Jesus' genealogy runs from Abraham to David and on to Christ, showing that God is faithful to keep his covenant.
Jesus is conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary, fulfilling the prophecy of Immanuel.
Joseph obeys God's instruction, takes Mary as his wife, and names Jesus.
chapters.application: God fulfills his promises through history. Let us trust his leading, obey his word in our ordinary lives, and experience his presence.

chapters.summary: After the birth of Jesus, wise men from the East come to worship him, Herod the king seeks to kill him, and Joseph's family flees to Egypt before finally settling in Nazareth.
keyPoints: The wise men from the East follow the star and offer gold, frankincense, and myrrh in worship of Jesus.
Fearing the newborn king, Herod the king slaughters the infants of Bethlehem, fulfilling the prophet's words.
Joseph, warned by the Lord, takes his family and flees to Egypt, later settling in Nazareth, fulfilling prophecy.
chapters.application: In times of turmoil, let us trust in God's guidance - he will keep us, just as he kept the infant Jesus.

chapters.summary: John the Baptist preaches in the wilderness to prepare the way for Jesus; when Jesus is baptized, heaven opens, the Spirit descends, and the Father declares Jesus to be his beloved Son.
keyPoints: John the Baptist calls people to repent and prepare the way of the Lord, emphasizing the importance of a changed heart.
John points out the hypocrisy of the Pharisees and the Sadducees, warning them to bear fruit worthy of repentance.
Jesus is baptized, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father's voice confirms his identity and mission.
chapters.application: Let us examine ourselves each day, living out repentance through action, and hold fast to the assurance that Jesus is the Son of God, finding strength and hope in him.

chapters.summary: Jesus is tempted by the devil in the wilderness; having overcome temptation, he begins to preach, calls his disciples, and heals the people, revealing the power of the kingdom of heaven.
keyPoints: Jesus fasts forty days and forty nights and overcomes the devil's temptations, showing his resolve to obey God.
Jesus begins to preach and calls Peter, Andrew, and other disciples to become fishers of men.
Jesus travels throughout Galilee, teaching, preaching the gospel, and healing every kind of sickness, and his fame spreads far and wide.
chapters.application: When we face temptation, let us follow Jesus' example and resist with the word of God; let us also answer his call, being salt and light in our lives and spreading the gospel.

chapters.summary: On the mountain, Jesus teaches his disciples the ethics of the kingdom of heaven, covering the Beatitudes, salt and light, the law, hatred, adultery, divorce, oaths, retaliation, and loving one's enemies.
keyPoints: The Beatitudes reveal the character and blessings of the people of the kingdom of heaven - such as being poor in spirit, mourning, and meekness.
Believers are the salt and light of the world, called to glorify God through good works.
Jesus fulfills the law, emphasizing that the heart's motives matter more than outward actions.
chapters.application: In our daily lives, let us pursue purity of heart, treat others with gentleness and compassion, and respond even to our enemies with love, becoming light that shines in the world.

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches his disciples the right attitude toward giving, prayer, and fasting, emphasizing that they should seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and not worry about tomorrow.
keyPoints: Giving, prayer, and fasting should be done in secret, not seeking people's praise but the Father's reward.
The Lord's Prayer teaches us the priorities and content of prayer, including God's glory, our daily needs, and forgiveness.
Do not store up treasures on earth, but store up treasures in heaven, for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
chapters.application: Let us draw near to God in secret each day, putting his kingdom and righteousness first. We need not worry about life, for our heavenly Father will surely care for us.

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches his disciples about judging others, asking in prayer, the narrow gate, false prophets, and the importance of doing the will of the Father.
keyPoints: Do not judge others, lest you be judged; first take the log out of your own eye.
Ask, and it will be given you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you - the heavenly Father will give good things.
Enter through the narrow gate and walk the narrow road; beware of false prophets, for only those who do the will of the Father will enter the kingdom of heaven.
themes: The Marks of a True Disciple
chapters.application: Let us examine ourselves today, avoid criticizing others carelessly, pray more and depend on God, and resolve to walk in the Lord's way, becoming true disciples who bear fruit.

chapters.summary: Jesus performs miracles in Galilee, revealing his authority, calling disciples, and teaching the cost of following him.
keyPoints: Jesus cleanses a leper, revealing his compassion and power.
A centurion asks the Lord in faith, and Jesus commends his faith.
Jesus calms the storm, and the disciples marvel at his authority.
chapters.application: When facing storms in life, let us depend on Jesus in faith, for he governs all things, and his compassion and power are enough to help us.

chapters.summary: Jesus heals and forgives sins in Galilee, calls Matthew to be his disciple, and responds to the questions of the Pharisees, revealing his authority and compassion.
keyPoints: Jesus heals a paralyzed man, showing that he has authority to forgive sins.
Jesus calls the tax collector Matthew and eats with sinners, showing that he came to call sinners.
Jesus answers questions about fasting, using the parable of new cloth and old garments to illustrate the difference between the new and the old.
themes: The Renewal of the New and Old
chapters.application: Today, let us follow Jesus' example of compassion, welcome those on the margins, and boldly answer his call, experiencing his renewal in our life of faith.

chapters.summary: Jesus sends out the twelve disciples to preach, giving them authority, and teaches them how to face persecution, along with his promises to them.
keyPoints: Jesus gives his disciples authority to cast out demons and heal diseases, and sends them to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
The disciples are to depend on the Holy Spirit as they preach, taking no purse or bag, for the laborer deserves his food.
In the face of persecution, do not be afraid; be wise as serpents and innocent as doves, and acknowledge the Lord's name, for he will also acknowledge us.
chapters.application: We are called to proclaim the gospel. Let us depend on God in faith, unafraid of our circumstances, boldly bearing witness to the Lord's name, for he will surely watch over us and give us our reward.

chapters.summary: This chapter records John the Baptist's question, Jesus' testimony about him, Jesus' rebuke of the cities that rejected the gospel, and his invitation for people to come to him for rest.
keyPoints: John the Baptist sends men to ask Jesus whether he is the one who is to come, and Jesus answers with the miracles he has done.
Jesus says that John is the greatest among the prophets, yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
Jesus rebukes Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum for their failure to repent, and invites people to take up his yoke.
chapters.application: When our faith wavers, let us remember the Lord's gracious work in our lives; and let us come to him with our labors and burdens, for he will surely give us rest.

chapters.summary: Jesus heals on the Sabbath and explains his authority over the Sabbath; he refutes the Pharisees' accusation that he casts out demons by the prince of demons, and emphasizes that doing the will of God is what makes one truly family.
keyPoints: Jesus is the Lord of the Sabbath - the Son of man is Lord of the Sabbath - and his disciples plucking heads of grain does not break the Sabbath.
Jesus heals on the Sabbath, and the Pharisees accuse him; he quotes the prophet to show that God desires mercy.
Jesus refutes the false charge that he casts out demons by the prince of demons, and warns that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
chapters.application: When we face conflict between rules and human need, let us follow Jesus' example, acting out of compassion and love, and never let rules blind us to people's needs.

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven through parables, explaining the parables of the sower and the weeds, and points out that a prophet is not honored in his own hometown.
keyPoints: The parable of the sower shows that different hearts yield different results, and only good soil produces a hundredfold.
The parable of the weeds reveals that at the judgment of the last days, the righteous will shine like the sun, while the wicked will be gathered and burned.
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure and a pearl, worth selling everything to obtain, showing its priceless value.
chapters.application: Let us examine our own attitude toward hearing God's word, becoming good soil so that his word takes root and bears fruit; and let us treasure the value of the kingdom of heaven, willing to give up everything to follow the Lord.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the death of John the Baptist at the hand of Herod, and Jesus' miracles of feeding the five thousand with five loaves and two fish and walking on the sea, revealing his power and compassion.
keyPoints: Herod imprisons John the Baptist for rebuking him over his marriage to his brother's wife, and finally has John killed at his birthday feast through Herodias' scheme.

When Jesus hears the news of John's death, he withdraws to a desolate place, but the crowds follow him; moved with compassion, he heals the sick, and then feeds five thousand people with five loaves and two fish.
At night the disciples encounter a storm on the sea; Jesus walks on the water, and Peter also tries to walk toward him but sinks because of his little faith - Jesus saves him and calms the storm.
chapters.application: In hardship, let us look to Jesus - he governs every storm. Even when our faith is small, he still reaches out to hold us up and gives us grace enough.

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches that true cleanness is a matter of the heart, shows compassion to the Canaanite woman, and feeds four thousand people.
keyPoints: The Pharisees question why the disciples do not wash their hands, and Jesus points out that they have set aside God's commandments for the sake of their traditions.
Jesus teaches that what goes into a person's mouth does not defile them, but what comes out of the mouth does, emphasizing the importance of the heart.
Jesus heals the Canaanite woman's daughter and feeds four thousand people, showing his compassion and provision.
chapters.application: Let us examine our hearts rather than clinging to outward forms, treat others with faith and compassion, and experience the Lord's abundant provision.

chapters.summary: Jesus warns the disciples to beware of the teaching of the Pharisees, reveals his identity, and foretells his suffering and resurrection.
keyPoints: The Pharisees demand a sign, but Jesus refuses and warns the disciples to beware of their leaven.
Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, and Jesus declares that he will build his church on this rock.
Jesus foretells his suffering and resurrection, and teaches the disciples to take up their cross and follow him.
chapters.application: In our daily lives, let us confess Jesus as the Christ and be willing to take up our own cross, deny ourselves, and follow him, making him the center of our lives.

chapters.summary: Jesus is transfigured on the mountain, revealing God's glory, and teaches the disciples lessons on faith and humility.
keyPoints: Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a mountain, where he is transfigured before them, his face shining like the sun.
Moses and Elijah appear and speak with Jesus about what he is about to accomplish in Jerusalem, and the Father declares that Jesus is his beloved Son.
After coming down the mountain, Jesus heals a boy possessed by a demon, teaches the disciples about faith as small as a mustard seed, and again foretells his suffering.
chapters.application: Trust in God's mighty power - even faith as small as a mustard seed can accomplish great things. Let us learn from Jesus' humility and serve others.

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches the disciples to be humble like little children, to deal seriously with sin within the church, and emphasizes the boundlessness of forgiveness.
keyPoints: The disciples must become humble like little children in order to be great in the kingdom of heaven.
Jesus warns of the seriousness of causing others to stumble, calling for sin to be dealt with decisively.
Church discipline and boundless forgiveness go hand in hand, reflecting the Father's mercy.
chapters.application: In our families and in the church, let us serve with humility, forgive one another seventy times seven, and lovingly restore those who have gone astray.

chapters.summary: Jesus teaches about marriage, divorce, celibacy, and children in the kingdom of heaven, and points out that it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom, though with God all things are possible.
keyPoints: Jesus reaffirms the sanctity of marriage, stressing that what God has joined together, no one should separate.
The disciples think it better not to marry, and Jesus explains that celibacy is a gift, not something everyone can receive.
Jesus blesses the little children and teaches that the kingdom of heaven belongs to those who are humble like them.
chapters.application: Let us keep our commitments in marriage, receive God's teaching with humility, and learn to trust God like a little child, not letting wealth hold us captive.

chapters.summary: Jesus uses the parable of the workers in the vineyard to teach about the fairness of the kingdom's grace, foretells his suffering again, and teaches the disciples that true greatness lies in serving others.
keyPoints: The workers in the vineyard all receive the same wage, showing that God's grace is not given according to human merit.
Jesus foretells his suffering and resurrection for the third time, but the disciples still do not understand.
The disciples argue about who is greatest, and Jesus teaches that whoever wants to be first must be a servant.
chapters.application: Let us not compare God's gifts with others, but receive them with gratitude. Let us follow Jesus' example, serving others in humility, and living out love in our families and in the church.

chapters.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem in glory, cleanses the temple, curses the fig tree, and debates authority and parables with the Jewish leaders, revealing his authority and judgment.
keyPoints: Jesus rides into the city on a donkey, fulfilling the prophet's words, as the crowds cry out 'Hosanna,' showing that he is the Messiah.
Jesus cleanses the temple, driving out the money changers and merchants, and rebukes them for turning a house of prayer into a den of robbers.
Through the parable of the fig tree and the parable of the two sons, Jesus teaches about faith and obedience, and points out the unbelief of the religious leaders.
chapters.application: Let us welcome Jesus as King with humble and obedient hearts, live out trust and purity in our daily lives, guard against a faith that is words without substance, and respond to God's call with action.

chapters.summary: Through parables and debate, Jesus teaches the truths of the kingdom of heaven, points out that the greatest commandment is to love God and love others, and declares that he is David's Lord.
keyPoints: The kingdom of heaven is like a king who gave a wedding feast for his son, but those invited refused to come, showing God's invitation and people's indifference toward it.

The Pharisees and the Sadducees test Jesus one after another with questions about paying taxes, the resurrection, and the law, and he answers each with wisdom and composure; finally he asks them how David could call the Christ his Lord, showing that his authority surpasses David's.
The greatest commandment is to love the Lord your God with all your heart and soul, and the second is like it: to love your neighbor as yourself.
chapters.application: Let us respond to God's call with gratitude, live out the commandment to love God and love others in our daily lives, and honor Christ as Lord.

chapters.summary: Jesus rebukes the hypocrisy of the scribes and the Pharisees, and laments Jerusalem's fate for rejecting the prophets.
keyPoints: Jesus points out that the scribes and the Pharisees say one thing and do another, loading heavy burdens onto people's shoulders.
They love ostentatious clothing and seats of honor in the synagogues, yet neglect the weightier matters of the law.
Jesus pronounces woes on the Pharisees and foretells that Jerusalem will be left desolate.
themes: The True Meaning of the Law
chapters.application: Let our words and actions be consistent, let us not seek empty praise, but serve others with humble hearts, and pray often for the repentance of our city and our people.

chapters.summary: Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple and the signs of the end times, urging the disciples to watch and be ready for the coming of the Son of man.
keyPoints: Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple, and the disciples ask about the signs of his coming and of the end of the age.
Jesus warns of false christs, wars, famines, and earthquakes, but says the end is not yet.
Believers must endure to the end, and only after the gospel has been preached to the whole world will the end come.
themes: The Faithful and the Wicked Servant
chapters.application: In the face of a turbulent world, let us hold fast to our faith, watch and pray, and wait for the Lord's return with faithfulness and love, so that we are not led astray.

chapters.summary: Through the parable of the ten virgins, the parable of the talents, and the parable of the sheep and the goats, this chapter teaches the disciples to watch and be ready, to be faithful in their responsibilities, and to care for their neighbors as they await the coming of the Son of man.
keyPoints: The parable of the ten virgins reminds believers to watch and be ready, for no one knows the day the Lord will come.
The parable of the talents teaches us to be faithful in using the gifts and resources God has entrusted to us, since we will one day give an account to him.
The parable of the sheep and the goats emphasizes that caring for the least of these brothers is caring for the Lord himself, and this is the standard of judgment.
chapters.application: Today, let us be faithful in the small things God has entrusted to us in daily life, reach out to those in need, and prepare to meet the Lord through our actions.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the final hours before Jesus' suffering, including Judas' betrayal, the Last Supper, his prayer in the garden of Gethsemane, and his arrest.
keyPoints: The chief priests and elders plot to kill Jesus, and Judas betrays him for thirty pieces of silver.
Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper, signifying that his body and blood would be given and poured out for many.
After praying in the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus is betrayed by Judas, who identifies him with a kiss.
chapters.application: In our daily lives, let us watch and pray, overcome temptation through the Lord, and remain faithful in small things, so as not to fail the trust he has placed in us.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how Jesus was handed over to Pilate, tried, condemned, crucified, and buried, fulfilling the prophets' words.
keyPoints: Judas regrets betraying Jesus and hangs himself, and the priests use the silver to buy a field.
Though Pilate knows Jesus is innocent, he gives in to the crowd's clamor, releases Barabbas, and hands Jesus over to be crucified.
Jesus is mocked and crucified; the curtain of the temple is torn in two, and the centurion confesses that he is the Son of God.
chapters.application: When we face injustice, let us follow Jesus' example of gentle submission, trust that God is sovereign over all things, and hold fast to our faith in the midst of suffering.

chapters.summary: This chapter records Jesus' resurrection, his appearances to the women and the disciples, and his giving of the Great Commission, encouraging the disciples to preach the gospel to the end of the age.
keyPoints: The women come to the tomb, an angel announces that Jesus has risen, and they meet the risen Lord.
The eleven disciples went to the mountain in Galilee as Jesus had directed, and when they saw him they worshipped him, though some among them still doubted.
He gives the Great Commission, commanding the disciples to make disciples of all nations, and promises to be with them always.
chapters.application: Jesus' resurrection gives us hope, and the Great Commission calls us to share the gospel. May we live out the resurrection life each day, boldly proclaim the Lord's love, and experience his presence.
